short: Affect decoded from silent-articulation EMG, a design absent from 99 ledger studies (M08, ahead); it works within subject, nears chance across speakers, and is not separated from facial expression.
position: The paper changes the output (M08) to an affect label decoded from facial and neck EMG during silent articulation, a design none of the 99 ledger studies on paralinguistic output from production signals has (Appendix); the closest priors decode speaker identity and speaking mode from EMG, analyse emotional articulation without an emotion classifier, or decode emotion in a silent-speech wearable from carotid pulse. The phonated-to-silent test (M04) is standard; the zero-shot BioCodec encoder loses little across modes. The claim that affect is carried by speech-motor activity is not established: the authors name a brow electrode as the most prominent site and concede that facial expression cannot be separated from articulation. Within-subject decoding works (AUC 0.845); unseen-speaker EMG AUC is 0.567 to 0.574, close to chance with no chance-level test, and spontaneous affect is decoded better from audio.
